# T228 Heavy-tailed stationary law of constant-step SGD for a nonlinear model

Lead: unassigned. Dossier written 2026-10-16 02:3x by claude-99aebc7f from the auditor's record (codex-w687, 02:21) and
a reading of 2006.04740 (Theorem 1, Proposition 5, Appendix C.6.4) and 2006.06293 (Theorem 1). Whoever takes the row
owns the dossier from then on.

## STATEMENT
Repaired statement (the list row named no model, loss, data law or noise; auditor codex-w687, 16 Oct, statement_ok NO).
Scalar single-neuron regression. Data a ~ N(0,1), label y = sigma(a x*) + eps with eps ~ N(0, s^2), s > 0, independent
of a. Loss f(x; a, y) = (sigma(a x) - y)^2 / 2. Constant-step minibatch SGD with batch b and step eta:
    x_{k+1} = Psi_k(x_k) = x_k - (eta/b) sum_{i<=b} sigma'(a_i x_k) (sigma(a_i x_k) - y_i) a_i,   fresh (a_i, y_i) each step.
Two activation classes:
  (A) asymptotically linear: sigma(z) = z + phi(z), phi in C^2, sup|phi'| < 1, and phi, z phi'(z), z phi''(z) bounded
      (example phi = c tanh, |c| < 1);
  (B) leaky ReLU: sigma(z) = max(z, beta z), 0 <= beta < 1.
Prove: (1) the chain has a unique stationary law pi; (2) t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) -> c0 with c0 > 0 (for (B): a constant
for each sign); (3) alpha is the positive root of an explicit moment equation in (eta, b); (4) alpha < 2 on a nonempty
set of (eta, b).

## FRONTIER
- Gurbuzbalaban-Simsekli-Zhu arXiv:2006.04740 (ICML 2021): linear regression (quadratic loss, Gaussian data): exact
  index from E|det-type moment| = 1 via Kesten-Goldie / Alsmeyer-Mentemeier; 0 < alpha < 2 on a stable step interval
  (Proposition 5); monotone in eta/b under Gaussian data (A3) and alpha >= 1 (Theorem 4). Their Theorem 1 restates
  Mirek (2011) for asymptotically linear random maps: if a stationary solution exists, |Psi(x) - M x| <= B,
  log|M| non-arithmetic, E|M|^alpha = 1, E B^alpha < oo, E|M|^alpha log+|M| < oo, then t^alpha P(|x| > t) -> c0 > 0.
- Hodgkinson-Mahoney arXiv:2006.06293: Lipschitz random maps with k|w - w*| - M <= |Psi(w) - Psi(w*)| <= K|w - w*|,
  E log K < 0, P(k > 1) > 0: geometric ergodicity, two-sided power-law bounds, E k^alpha = 1, E K^beta = 1,
  limsup t^(alpha+eps) P > 0 and limsup t^(beta-eps) P < oo for every eps > 0. Bounds only; not the exact index, not c0 > 0.
- Jiao-Keller-Ressel arXiv:2402.01382: homogenized SGD (a diffusion), explicit upper and lower bounds on the index.
- Raj-Zhu-Gurbuzbalaban-Simsekli arXiv:2310.18455: offline SGD has approximate power-law tails (quadratic losses).
- arXiv search 16 Oct 02:2x (five queries, newest first): nothing on an exact index for a nonlinear model.

## ARCHITECTURE
Write Psi(x) = M x + R(x). Class (A): the gradient is a^2 x + a (a x) phi'(a x) + a (1 + phi'(a x)) (phi(a x) - y), so
M = 1 - (eta/b) sum a_i^2 (the linear-regression multiplier) and |R(x)| <= B = (eta/b) sum |a_i| (C1 + C2 |y_i|).
Then: (i) existence and uniqueness of pi by a Foster drift V = |x|^p (small p, E|M|^p < 1) plus a minorization (the
label noise gives Psi_k(x) a Gaussian component of variance >= (eta/b)^2 s^2 (1 - sup|phi'|)^2 sum a_i^2 > 0, so
compact sets are small) -> positive Harris recurrence; (ii) Mirek's theorem for the limit; (iii) a separate argument
for c0 > 0; (iv) the moment equation E|1 - (eta/b) chi2_b|^alpha = 1, which is the linear one: the nonlinearity does
not move the index. Class (B): Psi(x) = M_{sgn x} x + Q_{sgn x} with M_+ = 1 - (eta/b) sum w(a_i)^2 a_i^2,
w(a) = 1{a > 0} + beta 1{a < 0}, M_- the same with -a_i: an affine recursion whose coefficients switch with the sign of
the state, i.e. a Markov-modulated Kesten recursion (Kesten 1974, renewal theory for functionals of a Markov chain).

## FAILURE POINT
Two places. (1) c0 > 0 is not delivered by any theorem in hand. GSZ's restatement of Mirek asserts c0 > 0 under
(i)-(iii) alone, and that is false as written: Psi(x) = M sgn(x) (|x| - K)^+ satisfies (i) with B = |M| K, (ii) and
(iii) for suitable M, and delta_0 is its unique stationary law, so c0 = 0. Whatever nondegeneracy Mirek actually assumes
(read Mirek, PTRF 2011, Theorems 1.8 and 1.15, which GSZ's Appendix C.6.4 cites) has to be verified for the GLM.
Hodgkinson-Mahoney give only limsup t^(alpha+eps) P > 0. (2) For class (B) the map is not asymptotically linear in
Mirek's sense (the multiplier depends on sgn x), so Theorem 1 does not apply at all; Hodgkinson-Mahoney give bounds
with k = min(|M_+|, |M_-|) and K = max, which differ.

## SHAPE
DAYS for class (A): every step is a known tool; the work is checking hypotheses, plus a positivity lemma (the Gaussian
label noise gives the stationary law a density everywhere and unbounded support, which is the natural input).
Days to weeks for class (B): the index guess is explicit. By the symmetry a -> -a, M_+ and M_- have the same law, so
the 2x2 matrix Lambda(s)_{sigma,tau} = E[|M_sigma|^s 1{sgn(M_sigma) sigma = tau}] has both row sums E|M_+|^s and
spectral radius E|M_+|^s: conjecturally alpha solves E|1 - (eta/b) sum w(a_i)^2 a_i^2|^alpha = 1. The work is
verifying Kesten's Markov-renewal hypotheses (the sign chain is a two-state chain driven by the same Omega as the
increments, so the modulation is not independent of the jumps).

## OBSTRUCTION
What makes the general problem hard is the growth of Psi, not the tail theory. Bounded activations (tanh, sigmoid)
give a gradient bounded by C |a| (1 + |y|) uniformly in x: with weight decay the recursion is a deterministic
contraction plus light-tailed noise (light tails); without it there is no contraction (M = 1). Two-layer networks give
cubic growth of Psi in the parameters; with Gaussian inputs and a constant step the chain then plausibly escapes to
infinity almost surely (from size R a step multiplies by about eta a^2 R^2, and the chance of not doing so is
summable along a geometric escape) - an argument sketch, not written up - so no stationary law exists to have a tail.
So Kesten-type heavy tails need activations of linear growth (class A, leaky ReLU) or bounded inputs. Moves: an exact
index with c0 > 0 for one honest nonlinear model; the sign-modulated index for leaky ReLU; d dimensions.

## SETTLED
- Linear regression: exact index, alpha < 2 range, monotonicity under (A3) and alpha >= 1 (GSZ 2006.04740).
- General Lipschitz maps: two-sided bounds only (Hodgkinson-Mahoney 2006.06293, Theorem 1).
- GSZ Theorem 1 as restated (c0 > 0 from (i)-(iii) plus existence) is false without a nondegeneracy hypothesis; the
  counterexample is in FAILURE POINT. Read Mirek's own statement before citing it.
- Scalar b = 1, unit-variance Gaussian a, class (A): alpha < 2 iff E(1 - eta a^2)^2 > 1 iff eta > 2/3, and
  E log|1 - eta a^2| < 0 on the whole of [0.3, 2.0] (numerical quadrature, 16 Oct: -0.49 at 0.6, -0.42 at 1.0,
  -0.12 at 2.0). For batch b the threshold is eta > 2b/(b + 2); E log|M| < 0 at eta = 2 for b = 1, 2, 4, 8. So (4) holds
  on a nonempty interval once (1)-(3) are proved.
- NOT moves: another linear model; numerical tail-index estimates for networks; heavy-tailed additive noise (that is
  the input's tail, not the multiplicative mechanism).

## TARGETS
1. Class (A), scalar: prove (1)-(4) in full, with c0 > 0. Expected index: the linear one, E|1 - (eta/b) chi2_b|^alpha = 1.
   Days. DONE under the stability condition (S) E log|1 - (eta/b) chi2_b| < 0: w688-T228-A/L v1, accepted by claude-b1e26540
   16 Oct 06:44 (brain_workers/w688/T228/AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv). (S) is necessary: at b = 2, eta = 100 the index equation
   has no root.
2. Class (B), leaky ReLU, scalar: the stationary tail under the sign-modulated recursion, index from E|M_+|^alpha = 1 by
   the symmetry above; constants c0+ and c0- for the two signs. The first activation used in practice with an exact
   index.
3. Class (A) in R^d with a ~ N(0, I_d): M = I - (eta/b) sum a_i a_i^T, |R| bounded as in d = 1; Mirek's d-dimensional
   theorem or Alsmeyer-Mentemeier with the asymptotically linear perturbation. Index equals GSZ's linear one.
   DONE 22 Oct under (S_d) E log xi < 0: claude_b1e26540/T3_CLAIM.md v2, reviewed by claude-4af6ff1a and claude-fc67971c.
NOT targets: two-layer networks with Gaussian inputs at constant step (see OBSTRUCTION: likely transient).

## 2026-10-21 19:3x claude-4af6ff1a: TARGET 2 submitted (v1, not yet reviewed)
claude_4af6ff1a/T228_B_v1.md: leaky ReLU, any beta in [0,1), (S') E log|A+|<0. The map is piecewise affine and A- has the law of A+, so the multiplier the chain uses is independent of the state (the SHAPE paragraph above calls the modulation dependent; it is harmless). content:
# Frontier rules for a solver on a top-200 row

These replace "improve what you can certify". F below is
`python -X utf8 ~/<private-repo>/06_math_research/frontier/frontier.py`.

1. Start from the frontier, not from our history. Your first action is `F brief TNNN` and reading it in full: the
   statement, the frontier papers, how their proof goes, the exact place it fails, the obstruction, what is settled and
   the targets. Then read the frontier paper's own pages at the failure point. Earlier attempts by our workers appear
   only as settled facts and dead routes; do not go looking for more of them.
2. Before you start any route or lemma, run `F check TNNN "<the route in one sentence>"`.
   Exit 2: a settled fact or a dead route matches. Do not redo it; read the evidence. You may go on only with a
   concrete reason it differs, written into your ROUTES.jsonl line. Exit 1: someone holds or claimed something close;
   build on it. Exit 0: go ahead.
3. Keep `ROUTES.jsonl` in your own folder, one line per route:
   {"row": "TNNN", "route": "<one sentence>", "status": "live" | "dead" | "done", "why": "<for dead: the precise
   reason, with the witness or the failing step>", "evidence": "<claim id or file>", "at": "<ISO time>"}.
   Open a route as live when you start it; close it as dead or done when you stop. A dead route without a why is
   useless to the next worker.
4. Every CLAIMS.jsonl entry carries two more fields: "kind" - one of moved, narrowed, special, bound, literature,
   route-failure - and "target" - the TARGETS number in the dossier it serves, or "none".
   moved: a step of the frontier architecture now goes through where it failed. narrowed: the statement itself is
   proved on a whole new part of its range (a parameter interval, an infinite family). Everything else is recorded but
   does not count as progress on the row.
5. Work the TARGETS in their order. A sharper constant, a further isolated case or a better certified bound that is
   not a named target is not the job, however cleanly it certifies. If you think a target is wrong or a better one
   exists, write why in STATUS.md; the lead decides.
6. Your STATUS.md NEXT line names the target number you are on.
7. A literature finding that answers the row or a target outranks everything: stop, write it as a claim of kind
   literature with the locator, and say so in STATUS.md.

name: claude_4af6ff1a/T228_B_v2.md
content:
# T228 target 2: scalar leaky-ReLU SGD has an exact power tail

claude-4af6ff1a, 21 Oct 2026. Version 2: version 1 (sha256 534eee207240ef79...) reviewed PASS with three wording
fixes by claude-b1e26540 (21 Oct 23:1x); the fixes are in the theorem's gamma = 0 sentence, in section 3 and in section 5.

## Setting
- Leaky ReLU: sigma(z) = max(z, beta z) with 0 <= beta < 1.
- Data: a ~ N(0,1) and y = sigma(a x*) + eps, with eps ~ N(0, s^2), s > 0, independent of a.
- Step: x_{k+1} = Psi_k(x_k) = x_k - c sum_{i<=b} sigma'(a_i x_k)(sigma(a_i x_k) - y_i) a_i, where c = eta/b and each
  step uses fresh i.i.d. samples (a_i, y_i), i <= b.
- Derivative: sigma'(z) = 1 for z > 0 and beta for z < 0. The value gamma := sigma'(0) may be any number in [beta, 1].
- Notation: w(a) = 1{a>0} + beta 1{a<0} and S_+ = sum_i w(a_i)^2 a_i^2, S_- = sum_i w(-a_i)^2 a_i^2.
- Slopes: A^+ = 1 - c S_+ and A^- = 1 - c S_-.
- Offsets: Q^+ = c sum_i w(a_i) a_i y_i and Q^- = c sum_i w(-a_i) a_i y_i.

**Theorem.** Assume (S'): E log|A^+| < 0. If gamma > 0, the chain has exactly one stationary law pi. If gamma = 0
(possible only when beta = 0), it has exactly two extremal stationary laws, delta_0 and one law pi on R \ {0}, and the
stationary laws are exactly l delta_0 + (1-l) pi, 0 <= l <= 1. In both cases, with kappa > 0 the
unique positive root of E|1 - c S_+|^kappa = 1,

    t^kappa pi((t, oo)) -> C   and   t^kappa pi((-oo, -t)) -> C,

with the same constant C > 0 for both signs. If (S') fails there is no root and the conclusion fails as stated (for
beta -> 1, target 1's counterexample at b = 2, eta = 100 applies). kappa < 2 holds on a nonempty interval of c for every
b and every beta (section 5).

The index does not depend on the sign of x, and neither does the constant. This holds even though the offsets do
depend on the sign: Q^+ and -Q^- are not equal in law when x* != 0. The dossier's SHAPE paragraph treats the sign as a
Markov modulation that is not independent of the jumps. In fact the multiplier chosen by the sign is independent of
the current state (section 2), so the modulation is harmless.

## 1. The map is piecewise affine
- For x > 0: a_i x > 0 exactly when a_i > 0. So sigma'(a_i x) = w(a_i) and sigma(a_i x) = w(a_i) a_i x, which gives
  Psi(x) = A^+ x + Q^+.
- For x < 0, likewise: Psi(x) = A^- x + Q^-.
- At x = 0: Psi(0) = c gamma sum_i a_i y_i.

So ABB's standing bound (4), sup_x |Psi(x) - Lambda(x)| <= B with Lambda(x) = A^{sgn x} x, holds with
B = max(1, c sum_i |a_i||y_i|), since w <= 1 and gamma <= 1. Since |y_i| <= |x*||a_i| + |eps_i|, B has moments of every
order, and so do A^+ and A^-.

Psi is continuous except at 0. Its one-sided limits there are Q^+ and Q^-, which differ when beta < 1. ABB's assumption
(1) (Psi a.s. continuous) therefore fails at the single point 0; section 4 deals with this.

## 2. The key symmetry
Write N = (a_1..a_b). Then S_- is S_+ evaluated at -N, and -N has the law of N, so A^- has the same law as A^+ =: A.

Let x be independent of the step's data and put m := A^{sgn x} (A^+ when x = 0). For Borel sets D and E,

    P(m in D, x in E) = P(A^+ in D) P(x in E, x >= 0) + P(A^- in D) P(x in E, x < 0) = P(A in D) P(x in E).

So the multiplier the chain actually uses is independent of the current state and has a fixed law, whatever the sign.
The offset q := Q^{sgn x} is not independent of x; nothing below needs it to be.

## 3. Existence, uniqueness and moments
- **Root.** The function h(q) = E|A|^q is finite for all q >= 0, strictly log-convex (A is not a.s. of constant
  modulus), h(0) = 1 and h'(0) = E log|A| < 0. Since P(|A| > 1) > 0, h(q) -> oo. So there is exactly one kappa > 0
  with h(kappa) = 1, and h < 1 on (0, kappa).
- **Drift.** Take p in (0, min(1, kappa)). By section 2 and subadditivity,
  E|Psi(x)|^p <= h(p)|x|^p + E B^p with h(p) < 1. This is Foster's condition for V = 1 + |x|^p.
- **Minorization.** Fix K and C0 = [-K, K].
  - For x in (0, K], use the event E1 = {a_i in [1, 2] for all i}. Given N on E1, Psi(x) is Gaussian with mean
    bounded uniformly in x in C0 and variance c^2 s^2 sum_i a_i^2 >= c^2 s^2 b.
  - For x in [-K, 0), use E2 = {a_i in [-2, -1] for all i}, where w(-a_i) = 1. This gives the same bounds.
  - When gamma > 0, x = 0 is covered by the same events: there Psi(0) is Gaussian with variance at least
    (c gamma s)^2 b.
  - So P(x, .) >= delta Leb(. ∩ C0) for x in C0, and the chain is Lebesgue-irreducible and aperiodic.
  - For beta > 0, P(x, .) has a density for every x != 0 (and for x = 0 when gamma > 0): given N, Q^{sgn x} carries the
    Gaussian term c sum_i w(±a_i) a_i eps_i with variance c^2 s^2 S_± > 0.
  - For beta = 0 it does not. When every a_i has the wrong sign (probability 2^-b), S_± = 0 and Q^± = 0, so Psi(x) = x:
    P(x, .) = 2^-b delta_x + (an absolutely continuous part). Irreducibility and aperiodicity come from the
    minorization and are unaffected.
  - Positive Harris recurrence then gives a unique invariant pi. It is absolutely continuous: write pi = pi_a + pi_s
    (Lebesgue decomposition). Only the atoms delta_x contribute to the singular part of pi P, so pi_s = 2^-b pi_s for
    beta = 0 (and pi_s = 0 directly for beta > 0); hence pi_s = 0. The minorization on every C0 gives full support; in
    particular the support is unbounded and pi({0}) = 0.
- **The case gamma = 0, beta = 0.** Psi(0) = 0, so delta_0 is invariant. From x != 0, P(Psi(x) = 0) = 0 (the atom of
  P(x, .) sits at x, the rest is absolutely continuous), so R \ {0} is absorbing and avoids 0. The argument above, run
  on R \ {0}, gives the second law pi. The state space splits into the two absorbing sets {0} and R \ {0}, each with a
  unique invariant law, so every stationary law is l delta_0 + (1-l) pi and the two are the extremal ones.
- **Moments.** E_pi|x|^r < oo for every r < kappa. Run the chain from x_0 = 1. Section 2 applies at every step
  because the step's data is independent of x_k. So
  - ||x_{k+1}||_r <= h(r)^{1/r} ||x_k||_r + ||B||_r for r >= 1 (Minkowski);
  - E|x_{k+1}|^r <= h(r) E|x_k|^r + E B^r for r < 1.

  Hence sup_k E|x_k|^r < oo. Since x_k converges to pi in total variation, Fatou finishes.

## 4. The tail: ABB Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 8.1, with continuity replaced
**The Cramer matrix.** ABB's matrix (8) has
- p_{--} = E|A^-|^t 1{A^->0} and p_{-+} = E|A^-|^t 1{A^-<0};
- p_{+-} = E|A^+|^t 1{A^+<0} and p_{++} = E|A^+|^t 1{A^+>0}.

Since A^- and A^+ have the same law, this is [[d, o], [o, d]] with d(t) = E|A|^t 1{A>0} and o(t) = E|A|^t 1{A<0}.
- P(A < 0) > 0 (A < 0 whenever S_+ > 1/c, and S_+ is unbounded), so this is the irreducible Case 1.
- rho(t) = d + o = h(t), so (12) is h(kappa) = 1.
- The eigenvectors are u = (1/2, 1/2) and v = (1, 1).
- (13): the moments in section 1.
- (14): the self transitions (A > 0) have positive tilted probability, and on them log A has an absolutely continuous
  part. This holds even for beta = 0, where A = 1 with probability 2^-b: A is continuous on {0 < S_+ < 1/c}, an event of
  positive probability. An absolutely continuous increment lies in a shifted lattice with probability 0, so the lattice
  event has probability < 1.

**Conclusion.** Theorem 2.1 gives the limits (15) for any stationary law, with u_+ C_- = u_- C_+ by (16), so C_+ = C_-.
Proposition 8.1 gives C_+, C_- > 0, because pi has unbounded support.

**Continuity.** ABB's hypothesis (1) (Psi a.s. continuous) fails at x = 0. In the arXiv v2 text (sha256 ec099b50...,
the same file as w688's source) the word "continuous" applied to Psi occurs only at:
- (1) itself, used for "has the Feller property" (line after (2));
- Prop. 9.1, the existence of a stationary law ("is also a Feller chain").

Sections 3-8 (the comparison with the linear system Lambda, the Markov renewal argument, the proofs of Theorem 2.1 and
Proposition 8.1) work with (4), Lip(Lambda_n) and the invariance of nu, for ANY stationary distribution nu. Existence
here comes from section 3 (Harris), not from Feller. So the jump at the single point 0 is never used. REVIEW POINT 1:
check this reading of ABB sections 3-8, in particular that no step uses continuity of Psi (as opposed to Lambda) or the
Feller property.

**Fallback if a reviewer finds continuity used.** Section 2 makes Goldie's implicit renewal theorem (Ann. Appl. Probab.
1991, Thm 2.3, the case P(M < 0) > 0) apply directly, with M = m independent of R ~ pi:
- the two difference integrals are at most E|((mR+q)^+)^k - ((mR)^+)^k|/k, finite by the moments of section 3;
- this gives both limits, equal to the same C >= 0, with no continuity hypothesis;
- only C > 0 would then rest on ABB section 8.

## 5. kappa < 2 on an interval
Let mu = E w(a)^2 a^2 = (1+beta^2)/2 and nu4 = E w(a)^4 a^4 = 3(1+beta^4)/2. Then

    E A^2 = 1 - 2 c b mu + c^2 (b nu4 + b(b-1) mu^2),

so E A^2 > 1 exactly when c > c_0 := 2 mu / (nu4 + (b-1) mu^2).

At c = c_0, Jensen gives E log|A| <= (1/2) log E A^2 = 0, with strict inequality because |A| is not a.s. constant.
E A^2 is a polynomial in c. For E log|1 - cS_+|: S_+ has an atom at 0 only (where the integrand is 0) and otherwise a
density f bounded on compact subsets of (0, oo), so for c in a compact subset of (0, oo), substituting u = cs gives
E log|1 - cS_+| = ∫ log|1 - u| f(u/c) c^-1 du (the atom contributes 0), and dominated convergence (log|1 - u| is locally
integrable, f(u/c)/c is bounded near u = 1 uniformly in c, and log(1 + u) dominates the tail against the moments of
S_+) makes it continuous in c. Both sides are therefore continuous in c, so on (c_0, c_0 + delta) we have (S'), h(2) > 1, and hence kappa < 2. This holds for every
b >= 1 and every beta in [0, 1).

## 6. Numbers (support only, not proof): leaky_index_run1.txt
- The root kappa (4e6 draws): beta 0.1, b 1, eta 1.0 gives kappa 1.118; beta 0.5, b 4, eta 2.5 gives 1.077.
- c_0 at beta 0.1, b 1 is 0.673, matching E A^2 = 0.87 at c 0.5 and 1.49 at c 1.0.
- Simulated chains (20,000 chains, 3,000 steps) give Hill estimates of 1.26 and 1.11 against kappa 1.118 and 1.077.
  The first is biased upward, as Hill estimates are near kappa ~ 1 at these levels.
- Of the 200 largest |x|, 93 and 103 are positive, consistent with C_+ = C_- although x* = 1 breaks the x -> -x
  symmetry.

## Review record
claude-b1e26540, 21 Oct 23:1x, on version 1: PASS with three wording fixes, all applied above (the atom of P(x, .) at
beta = 0, the extremal laws at gamma = 0, the continuity of c -> E log|1 - cS_+|). The reviewer re-derived sections 1-5
by hand, read ABB's text for the sign convention of Lambda and matrix (8), agreed with review point 1 (Harris
existence replaces Feller; Theorem 2.1 holds for any stationary law) and rechecked c_0 = 0.6733 and E A^2 = 0.870 / 1.490.
Verdict on the dossier: TARGET 2 done under (S'), as target 1 was under (S): items (1)-(4) for class (B), with C_+ = C_-.

No novelty claim beyond the dossier's search of 16 Oct; that search is to be rerun before any paper.

# T228 target 3: class (A) single-index SGD in R^d. Claim, version 2

claude-b1e26540, 22 Oct 2026 04:5x (v1), 05:2x (v2). STATE: VERIFIED (two independent reviews). First review by claude-4af6ff1a
(REVIEW.tsv, 22 Oct 02:09Z): 16 PASS, 0 FIX, 0 FAIL; its one OPEN row (novelty) is answered in T3_NOVELTY.md. Second
review by claude-fc67971c (REVIEW.tsv, 22 Oct 04:06Z, commit 06966f6ae36): Theorems 2 and 3 re-derived by hand, all PASS,
no FIX; its own script (rows/T228/claude_fc67971c/audit2_check.py) gives alpha 1.3005 and c0 2.225 +- 0.023 at
(d, b, eta) = (2, 1, 0.6), and at (3, 2, 0.9), alpha 0.3578, c0 1.595 +- 0.013 against 1.572 here, with the empirical
tail still drifting at that small alpha. The mathematics is unchanged from v1.

## Model
d >= 1, b >= 1, eta > 0, c = eta/b. Each step draws fresh a_i ~ N(0, I_d) and eps_i ~ N(0, s^2), i <= b, s > 0, with
y_i = sigma(a_i.x*) + eps_i, and sets
    x_(k+1) = Psi_k(x_k) = x_k - c sum_(i<=b) sigma'(a_i.x_k) (sigma(a_i.x_k) - y_i) a_i.
Class (A): sigma(z) = z + phi(z) with r := sup|phi'| < 1, sup|phi| < oo and sup|z phi'(z)| < oo (the dossier's class (A)
assumes more: phi in C^2 and z phi'' bounded; those are not used).

Put xi := sqrt((1 - cX)^2 + c^2 X Y) with X ~ chi2_b and Y ~ chi2_(d-1) independent (Y = 0 when d = 1), h(p) = E xi^p, and
assume
    (S_d)  gamma := E log xi < 0.

## Theorem
Under class (A), s > 0 and (S_d):
 (1) the chain has a unique invariant probability pi; it has a density bounded below on every ball, and P^n(x, .) -> pi
     geometrically fast in the (1 + |x|^p)-weighted norm for every p < alpha;
 (2) t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) -> c0 with 0 < c0 < oo, where
         c0 = E[ |Psi(x)|^alpha - |M x|^alpha ] / (alpha E[xi^alpha log xi]),   M = I - c sum a_i a_i^T,  x ~ pi independent;
     in particular E_pi |x|^p < oo exactly for p < alpha;
 (3) alpha is the unique positive root of E[ ((1 - cX)^2 + c^2 X Y)^(alpha/2) ] = 1;
 (4) for every (d, b), alpha < 2 on a nonempty interval of eta: E xi^2 = 1 - 2 eta + eta^2 (b + d + 1)/b, so alpha < 2
     iff eta > eta0 := 2b/(b + d + 1), and (S_d) holds on (eta0, eta0 + delta) for some delta > 0.
For d = 1 this is target 1's class (A) statement with an explicit c0.

## Where each part is proved
- Lemma R (|M u| =_d xi for every unit u, and the pairs (|M_k u_k|, B_k) are iid along the chain): T3_SETUP.md.
- (1), the index (Lemma 1), drift and minorization: T3_STEP1.md, Theorem 1. Uses Hairer-Mattingly Theorem 1.2
  (arXiv 0810.2777v1, read on the page).
- (2), existence of the limit and the formula for c0 >= 0: T3_STEP2.md, Theorem 2. Uses Goldie's implicit renewal
  theorem in the form of Jelenkovic-Olvera-Cravioto arXiv 1006.3295v5, Theorem 3.1 (read on the page).
- (2), c0 > 0 and the infinite alpha-moment: T3_STEP3.md, Theorem 3. Self-contained: forward radial bound, a tilted
  random walk, a last-exit decomposition of pi.
- (3): Lemma 1 of T3_STEP1.md with Lemma R.
- (4): T3_SETUP.md (c), (d): at eta0, h(2) = 1 and strict Jensen gives gamma < 0; continuity in eta.

## Why the known theorems do not already give it
Mirek (PTRF 2011), the source of GSZ Theorem 1, requires M in R_+ x K with K a subgroup of O(d), i.e. similarities;
I - c sum a a^T is not one when d >= 2. ABB (2102.02299) is on the real line. The new point is that Gaussian data make
|M_k u_k| independent of the direction u_k, so the norm of the d-dimensional chain is an exact one-dimensional implicit
renewal problem, and the positivity of c0 can be proved forward in time without operator norms.

## Checks done since v1
- Novelty (T3_NOVELTY.md): web search in three wordings found linear-regression results (GSZ 2006.04740, with a
  direction-dependent constant), general implicit-renewal frameworks and a scalar paper (ABB), but no statement for a
  nonlinear link in d >= 2 with a positive norm constant. Web only, not an arXiv full-text sweep.
- Numbers (t3_tail_check.py, t3_tail_check_run1.txt, seed 1; sigma = z + 0.5 tanh z, x* = e1, s = 1; 4,000 chains x
  100,000 steps, 19M thinned samples): at (d, b, eta) = (2, 1, 0.6) the root of h is alpha = 1.3015, Hill gives
  1.296-1.308 over k = 5.7k-190k, and c0 by the formula of (2) is 2.247 +- 0.007 against t^alpha P(|x| > t) = 2.23 at
  the 0.99, 0.999 and 0.9999 quantiles. At (2, 1, 0.8): alpha = 0.4023, Hill 0.399-0.410, c0 formula 1.401 against
  1.42-1.445 empirically (about 2 percent; slower second-order convergence at small alpha). At (3, 2, 0.9): alpha =
  0.3576, Hill 0.356-0.372 for k >= 19k (0.397 at k = 5.7k, where the few independent excursions per chain make it
  noisy), c0 formula 1.572 against 1.60 and 1.63 at the 0.99 and 0.999 quantiles (1.47 at 0.9999). The weakest of the
  three; consistent, not sharp. The reviewer's own control
  (review_4af6_tail_check.py, s = 0.5) gave alpha 1.299 and Hill 1.19-1.28 at (2, 1, 0.6).

## Still open
- A second independent audit.
- Goldie 1991 Theorem 2.3 read on its own page (the cited form is JOC Theorem 3.1 with N = 1).

# T228 target 3, step 3: the tail constant is strictly positive

claude-b1e26540, 22 Oct 2026 04:3x. Status: draft for review. Uses T3_SETUP.md (Lemma R), T3_STEP1.md (Lemma 1, Lemma 3,
Theorem 1) and T3_STEP2.md (Theorem 2). Hypotheses and notation as in T3_STEP1.md: class (A), s > 0, (S_d), alpha the
root of h(alpha) = E xi^alpha = 1, B the step bound with |R(x)| <= B.

## Theorem 3
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, liminf_{t -> oo} t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) > 0. Hence the constant of Theorem 2 satisfies
c0 > 0, so P_pi(|x| > t) ~ c0 t^(-alpha) with 0 < c0 < oo, and E_pi |x|^alpha = oo.

ABB (arXiv 2102.02299) prove the analogous statement, Proposition 8.1, by optional sampling for the backward composition
Psi_1 o ... o Psi_n. In R^d that route bounds the remainder by operator norms ||M_1 ... M_(k-1)||, whose sum is not a
Goldie perpetuity. The proof below runs the chain forward, where Lemma R makes the radial bound a scalar recursion with iid
coefficients, and replaces optional sampling by a last-exit decomposition of pi.

## Four ingredients

(I) Radial lower bound. Fix x_0 = y and run x_j = Psi_j(x_(j-1)). Put u_(j-1) = x_(j-1)/|x_(j-1)| (u = e_1 if x = 0),
xi_j = |M_j u_(j-1)|, and B_j the bound of step j (a function of the |a_i| and eps_i of step j only). Rotating every a_i
of step j maps the pair (|M_j u|, B_j) for direction u to the pair for any other direction, so given the past the pair has
one fixed law: (xi_j, B_j) are iid, independent of y, with xi_j =_d xi (Lemma R). Within a pair they are dependent. Since
|Psi_j(x)| >= |M_j x| - B_j = xi_j |x| - B_j and xi_j >= 0, induction gives, with r_j = |x_j|, S_j = sum_(i<=j) log xi_i,
    r_j >= e^(S_j) r_0 - W_j,    W_j = sum_(i<=j) e^(S_j - S_i) B_i = e^(S_j) sum_(i<=j) e^(-S_i) B_i.          (3.1)

(II) The tilted walk. Let Q make the pairs iid with law xi^alpha dP (a probability law since E xi^alpha = 1). Then on the
sigma-field F_n of the first n pairs dQ/dP = e^(alpha S_n), so for a stopping time tau of the pairs and G in F_tau,
    P(tau < oo, G) = E_Q[ e^(-alpha S_tau) ; tau < oo, G ].                                                    (3.2)
Under Q, X = log xi has mean E xi^alpha log xi = m_alpha in (0, oo) (T3_STEP2.md), so S_n -> oo Q-a.s. For 0 < theta < alpha,
    E_Q e^(-theta X) = E xi^(alpha - theta) = h(alpha - theta) < 1                                             (3.3)
by Lemma 1. Three consequences:
 (a) p_+ := Q(S_j > 0 for all j >= 1) > 0. Pick L with Q(inf_(j>=0) S_j > -L) >= 1/2 (S_n -> oo) and delta > 0 with
     q := Q(X > delta) > 0 (E_Q X > 0). With m > L/delta, on {X_1, ..., X_m > delta} we have S_j > 0 for j <= m and S_m > L,
     and the walk after m is independent with infimum above -L with probability >= 1/2. So p_+ >= q^m / 2.
 (b) Overshoot. Let tau_u = inf{n : S_n > u} and O_u = S_(tau_u) - u (finite Q-a.s.). Let U = sum_(n>=0) Q(S_n in .).
     By (3.3) and Chernoff, U((-oo, 1]) <= e^theta / (1 - h(alpha - theta)) =: C_U. For any a, every visit to [a, a+1]
     after the first lies within 1 of it, so U([a, a+1]) <= C_U. Dropping the condition that the maximum before n stays
     below u,
         Q(O_u > z) <= sum_(n>=1) E_Q[ 1{S_(n-1) <= u} Fbar(u + z - S_(n-1)) ] <= C_U sum_(k>=0) Fbar(z + k)
                    <= C_U ( Fbar(z) + int_z^oo Fbar ),    Fbar(v) = Q(X > v),
     uniformly in u >= 0, and the right side tends to 0 as z -> oo because E_Q X^+ < oo.
 (c) V := sum_(i>=1) e^(-S_i) B_i. For 0 < theta < min(alpha, 1), using that B_i is independent of S_(i-1),
         E_Q V^theta <= sum_i E_Q[e^(-theta S_(i-1))] E_Q[xi_i^(-theta) B_i^theta] = E[xi^(alpha-theta) B^theta] / (1 - h(alpha-theta)) < oo
     (Hoelder; B and xi have every positive moment). So Q(V > v) <= v^(-theta) E_Q V^theta -> 0.

(III) Last-exit decomposition. Let x_0 ~ pi, A Borel, D Borel with A cap D empty, sigma_A = inf{k >= 1 : x_k in A},
sigma_D likewise. For N >= 1 split {x_N in D} by the last time in [0, N-1] at which the chain is in A (the events are
disjoint for different times) and use stationarity:
    pi(D) = P_pi(x_N in D) >= sum_(k=1)^N P_pi(x_0 in A, x_1, ..., x_(k-1) not in A, x_k in D)
          -> int_A pi(dx) E_x[ #{ k < sigma_A : x_k in D } ] >= int_A pi(dx) P_x(sigma_D < sigma_A).              (3.4)
No recurrence theorem is used; only stationarity of pi.

(IV) Leaving the ball. Lemma 3 with R = 4K: for |x| <= K and Borel E, P(x, E) >= eps_(4K) Leb(E cap B_(4K)).

## Proof of Theorem 3
Fix K and z (chosen below) and let t > 4K. Take A = B_K = {|x| <= K}, D = {|x| > t}, and the annulus
G_K = {2K <= |y| <= 4K}, which misses A.

Step 1: from y in G_K. Put u = log(t/K), tau = tau_u, and
    F = {S_j > 0 for 1 <= j <= tau} cap {V <= K/2} cap {O_u <= z}  (on {tau < oo}).
Let F' be F with V replaced by its partial sum V_tau = sum_(i<=tau) e^(-S_i) B_i; then F' is in F_tau and contains F.
On F', by (3.1) with r_0 = |y| >= 2K, for 1 <= j <= tau:
    r_j >= e^(S_j) (2K - K/2) = (3K/2) e^(S_j) > 3K/2,
so the chain does not return to B_K before tau, and at j = tau, r_tau >= (3K/2) e^(S_tau) > (3K/2)(t/K) > t. So sigma_D <= tau < sigma_A.
By (3.2), S_tau <= u + z on F', and (a)-(c):
    P_y(sigma_D < sigma_A) >= P(tau < oo, F') >= e^(-alpha(u+z)) Q(F') >= e^(-alpha(u+z)) Q(F)
                           >= (K/t)^alpha e^(-alpha z) [ p_+ - Q(V > K/2) - sup_(u>=0) Q(O_u > z) ].
Choose z and then K so that the bracket is at least p_+/2 (possible by (b) and (c)).

Step 2: from x in B_K. One step lands in G_K with probability at least eps_(4K) Leb(G_K) by (IV), without visiting B_K, so by
the Markov property at time 1,
    P_x(sigma_D < sigma_A) >= eps_(4K) Leb(G_K) (p_+/2) e^(-alpha z) K^alpha t^(-alpha).

Step 3. By (3.4) and pi(B_K) > 0 (Theorem 1 (iii)),
    pi(|x| > t) >= pi(B_K) eps_(4K) Leb(G_K) (p_+/2) e^(-alpha z) K^alpha t^(-alpha)     for all t > 4K.
So liminf t^alpha pi(|x| > t) > 0. Theorem 2 gives the limit c0, so c0 > 0. If E_pi|x|^alpha were finite, then
t^alpha P(|x| > t) <= E[|x|^alpha ; |x| > t] -> 0, contradicting c0 > 0. QED

## Remarks
- No renewal theorem, no non-arithmetic condition and no Cramer-Lundberg asymptotic is used here; the lower bound needs only
  m_alpha > 0, h < 1 on (0, alpha) (Lemma 1) and the one-step minorization (Lemma 3). Non-arithmeticity enters only
  through Theorem 2, for the existence of the limit.
- The dependence between xi_j and B_j inside a pair is harmless: (3.1) is pathwise, Q tilts the pair's joint law, and (c)
  only uses that B_i is independent of the earlier pairs.
- The same proof gives, for any start y with |y| large, P_y(sup_j |x_j| > t) >= c (|y|/t)^alpha.

## Target 3 as it now stands (steps 1-3, all drafts for review)
For the class-(A) single-index SGD chain in R^d with Gaussian data, s > 0 and gamma = E log xi < 0: a unique stationary law
pi with full support and E_pi |x|^p < oo exactly for p < alpha, and
    P_pi(|x| > t) ~ c0 t^(-alpha),   c0 = E[ |Psi(x)|^alpha - |Mx|^alpha ] / (alpha E xi^alpha log xi) in (0, oo),
alpha the positive root of E xi^alpha = 1, xi^2 = (1 - cX)^2 + c^2 X Y, X ~ chi2_b, Y ~ chi2_(d-1).
Citations: Hairer-Mattingly Theorem 1.2 (step 1, read on the page, arXiv 0810.2777v1); Goldie through JOC Theorem 3.1
(step 2, read). Step 3 cites nothing.

# T228 target 3 (class A in R^d): setup and route

claude-b1e26540, 22 Oct 2026 02:4x. A setup note, not a claim. Numbers: t3_numcheck.py / t3_numcheck_run1.txt.

## Model
a_i ~ N(0, I_d), y_i = sigma(a_i.x*) + eps_i, eps_i ~ N(0, s^2), sigma(z) = z + phi(z) with phi as in class (A).
Psi(x) = x - c sum_{i<=b} sigma'(z_i)(sigma(z_i) - y_i) a_i, z_i = a_i.x, c = eta/b. Then Psi(x) = M x + R(x) with
M = I - c sum a_i a_i^T and R(x) = -c sum [z_i phi'(z_i) + (1+phi'(z_i))(phi(z_i) - y_i)] a_i, so
|R(x)| <= B := c sum |a_i| (C1 + C2 |y_i|) <= c sum |a_i| (C1' + C2(|x*||a_i| + |eps_i|)) =: B'.
B' depends on (a_i, eps_i) only through |a_i| and eps_i; all its moments are finite.

## Why neither theorem used for targets 1-2 applies
- Mirek, PTRF 2011, Assumption 1.6 (H1): M must take values in G = R_+^* x K, K a closed subgroup of O(d)
  (similarities). For d >= 2, M = I - c sum a a^T is symmetric with eigenvalues 1 - c lambda_j that differ a.s.,
  so it is not a similarity. Theorem 1.8 does not apply. (Read in w688_target1/sources/Mirek_0907.2261_selected.txt.)
- ABB (2102.02299) is a theorem on the real line.
- GSZ's d-dimensional linear result goes through Alsmeyer-Mentemeier / Kesten for AFFINE recursions only.

## Route: reduce the norm to Goldie's scalar implicit renewal theorem
Lemma R (rotation invariance). For every unit vector u, |M u| has the law of
    xi := sqrt((1 - cX)^2 + c^2 X Y),   X ~ chi2_b, Y ~ chi2_{d-1} independent
(write a_i = (a_i.u) u + a_i^perp; sum (a_i.u) a_i^perp is N(0, X I_{d-1}) given X). The pair (|M u|, (|a_i|, eps_i)_i)
also has a joint law that does not depend on u (O(d) acts on the a_i jointly and fixes |a_i|). Since M_k is independent
of F_k, the pair (xi_k, B'_k) := (|M_k u_k|, B'_k) with u_k = x_k/|x_k| (any fixed u on x_k = 0) is independent of F_k with
a fixed law: the pairs are iid. Consequences:
  (a) log|M_n...M_1 u| = sum log xi_j exactly; the top Lyapunov exponent is gamma = E log xi.
  (b) h(s) = lim (E||M_n...M_1||^s)^(1/n) = E xi^s (GSZ's formula, here with a one-line proof).
  (c) E xi^2 = 1 - 2 eta + eta^2 (b+d+1)/b, so alpha < 2 iff eta > 2b/(b+d+1) (d=1: the dossier's 2b/(b+2)).
      Checked by Monte Carlo at three (d,b,eta); quantiles of |M u| agree across three directions and the formula.
  (d) A nonempty alpha<2 window exists for every (d,b): at eta0 = 2b/(b+d+1), h(2)=1 and strict Jensen gives
      gamma < 0; continuity keeps gamma < 0 and h(2) > 1 on (eta0, eta0 + delta). The window shrinks with d:
      gamma > 0 already at eta = 0.3 for d=10, b=1 (threshold 0.167), so (S_d): E log xi < 0 is a real restriction.

Goldie 1991 (Ann. Appl. Probab. 1, 126-166), Theorem 2.3, applied to R = |x| under pi and M := xi_0 (independent of x_0
by Lemma R): needs E xi^alpha = 1, E xi^alpha log+ xi < oo, log xi non-arithmetic (xi has a density), and
    int_0^oo |P(|Psi(x)| > t) - P(xi |x| > t)| t^(alpha-1) dt  <=  E | |Psi(x)|^alpha - |M x|^alpha | / alpha  <  oo.
For alpha <= 1 the right side is <= E B^alpha. For alpha > 1 it is <= C E[B (|Mx| + B)^(alpha-1)]; condition on x and use
Hoelder with E|Mu|^alpha = 1 for every u: bounded by C (E B^alpha)^(1/alpha) E|x|^(alpha-1) + C E B^alpha, finite once
E_pi |x|^p < oo for p < alpha (drift below). Then t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) -> c0 = E[|Psi(x)|^alpha - |Mx|^alpha]/(alpha m_alpha),
m_alpha = E xi^alpha log xi, with c0 >= 0.

## Steps left (what a worker must write)
1. Existence/uniqueness of pi. Drift: E|Psi(x)|^p <= E(xi|x| + B)^p <= h(p)|x|^p + C, h(p) < 1 for 0 < p < alpha.
   Minorization differs from d = 1: given the a_i, the label noise moves Psi(x) only inside span{a_1..a_b}, rank
   b < d possible. Use the k-step kernel with kb >= d (noise directions from k steps, carried by the intermediate M's,
   span R^d a.s.) to get a k-step small set; then positive Harris recurrence and aperiodicity.
2. Goldie as above, with each hypothesis checked on the page of the source (Goldie 1991 Thm 2.3 and Lemma 9.x).
3. c0 > 0. The hard step; Goldie gives only c0 >= 0. Candidate: the scalar lower chain r_{k+1} = (xi_k r_k - B'_k)^+
   (iid pairs by Lemma R) satisfies r_k <= |x_k| when r_0 <= |x_0|; with pi of full support (the Gaussian noise),
   a first-passage / Cramer-Lundberg argument for the random walk sum log xi_j (exponential tilt by alpha) gives
   liminf t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) > 0. Compare ABB Proposition 8.1 (sources/ABB_2102.02299_selected.txt) before writing.
4. Direction (bonus): with x* = 0 everything is O(d)-equivariant and the tail direction is uniform on S^(d-1). For
   x* != 0 conjecture the same; Goldie does not give it.
5. Novelty search before any claim: the radial reduction is natural for rotation-invariant data and may be known
   (GSZ compute h(s) this way for the linear model; search 2021-2026 for nonlinear d-dimensional SGD tails).

# T228 target 3, step 1: existence, uniqueness and moments of the stationary law in R^d

claude-b1e26540, 22 Oct 2026 03:4x. Status: draft for review. Setup and notation: T3_SETUP.md. Numbers:
t3_step1_check.py / t3_step1_check_run1.txt.

## Hypotheses
Class (A) as in w688_target1/proofs/T228_A_v1.md: sigma(z) = z + phi(z) with r := sup|phi'| < 1, H := sup|phi| < oo,
D := sup|z phi'(z)| < oo. Put m = 1 - r > 0 and L = 1 + r, so m <= sigma' <= L. Data: a_i ~ N(0, I_d), eps_i ~ N(0, s^2)
with s > 0, y_i = sigma(a_i.x*) + eps_i, fresh and independent at every step; b >= 1, eta > 0, c = eta/b, d >= 1.
    Psi(x) = x + c sum_{i<=b} u_i a_i,   u_i = sigma'(a_i.x) (y_i - sigma(a_i.x)),
    Psi(x) = M x + R(x),   M = I - c sum a_i a_i^T,
    |R(x)| <= B := c sum |a_i| (D + L(2H + |a_i||x*| + |eps_i|))      (independent of x; all moments finite).
xi has the law of Lemma R: xi^2 = (1 - cX)^2 + c^2 X Y, X ~ chi2_b, Y ~ chi2_{d-1} independent, and |M u| =_d xi for
every unit u. h(p) := E xi^p.

(S_d)  gamma := E log xi < 0.

## Lemma 1 (the index alpha)
E|log xi| < oo, h is finite and log-convex on [0, oo), h(0) = 1, h'(0+) = gamma, and h(p) -> oo. Under (S_d) there is a
unique alpha > 0 with h(alpha) = 1, and h(p) < 1 for 0 < p < alpha.

Proof. xi <= 1 + cX + c sqrt(XY), so every positive moment is finite. For the lower tail, P(xi < t) <= P(|1 - cX| < t)
<= C_b t, since chi2_b has a density bounded near 1/c > 0; hence E log^- xi < oo. Log-convexity is Hoelder; the
derivative at 0 is dominated convergence (|xi^p - 1|/p <= |log xi| (1 + xi) for p <= 1). h(p) >= 2^p P(xi > 2) -> oo
because P(xi > 2) > 0. A log-convex function equal to 1 at 0, with negative slope there and tending to infinity,
crosses 1 exactly once more, and lies below 1 between. QED

## Lemma 2 (drift)
Fix p in (0, alpha) and V(x) = 1 + |x|^p. There are gamma_p < 1 and K_p < oo with
    E V(Psi(x)) <= gamma_p V(x) + K_p     for all x.

Proof. |Psi(x)| <= |Mx| + B, and E|Mx|^p = h(p) |x|^p by Lemma R.
p <= 1: (u + v)^p <= u^p + v^p gives E|Psi(x)|^p <= h(p)|x|^p + E B^p; take gamma_p = h(p), K_p = 1 - h(p) + E B^p.
p > 1: Minkowski in L^p gives (E|Psi(x)|^p)^(1/p) <= h(p)^(1/p) |x| + beta, beta = (E B^p)^(1/p). For delta > 0,
(u + v)^p <= (1+delta)^(p-1) u^p + (1 + 1/delta)^(p-1) v^p; choose delta with gamma_p := (1+delta)^(p-1) h(p) < 1.
No independence between M and B is used. QED

## Lemma 3 (one-step minorization on every ball, with the minorizing measure on the ball itself)
For every R > 0 there is eps_R > 0 such that for all |x| <= R and all Borel A,
    P(x, A) >= eps_R Leb(A cap B_R),     B_R = {|w| <= R}.

The rank of the noise is not an issue: one sample already moves Psi(x) along a Gaussian direction a_1, and the radius
along it is spread by eps_1. This replaces the k-step plan of T3_SETUP.md (kb >= d is not needed).

Proof. Write Psi(x) = x + S + c u_1 a_1 with S = c sum_{i>=2} u_i a_i (S = 0 when b = 1); S is independent of
(a_1, eps_1). Let G = {|a_i| <= 1, |eps_i| <= s for 2 <= i <= b}, of probability p_G > 0. Since |sigma(p) - sigma(q)|
<= L|p - q|, |u_i| <= L(L|a_i||x - x*| + |eps_i|), so on G, |S| <= S_R := c(b-1) L(L(R + |x*|) + s).
Polar coordinates for a_1: a_1 = rho_a theta with rho_a = |a_1| and theta uniform on S^{d-1} (normalized surface
measure omega), independent. Given (rho_a, theta) = (q, theta), the scalar t := c q u_1 is affine in eps_1 with slope
c q sigma'(q theta.x) != 0, so t is Gaussian with
    mean mu = c q sigma'(q theta.x)(sigma(q theta.x*) - sigma(q theta.x)),   sd tau = c q sigma'(q theta.x) s.
For q in [1, 2] and |x| <= R: |mu| <= 4 c L^2 (R + |x*|) =: mu_R and tau in [c m s, 2 c L s]. Hence for |t| <= T the
conditional density of t is at least
    g_lo(T) := (2 c L s sqrt(2 pi))^(-1) exp(-(T + mu_R)^2 / (2 c^2 m^2 s^2)) > 0.
For d >= 2 the map (theta, t) -> v = t theta is two-to-one from S^{d-1} x (R \ {0}) onto R^d \ {0}, with
Leb(dv) = |S^{d-1}| |t|^(d-1) dt omega(d theta) on each sheet. Keeping only the sheet t > 0, the density of v given
rho_a = q is at least g(|v| ; theta = v/|v|) / (|S^{d-1}| |v|^(d-1)), where g(. ; theta) is the conditional density of t.
(d = 1 is the scalar case of T228_A_v1: v = t theta with theta = +-1, and the same bound holds with |S^0| = 2, exponent 0.)
Now take |w| <= R. Then v := w - x - S satisfies |v| <= T_R := 2R + S_R on G, so the density of Psi(x) at w is at least
    eps_R := p_G P(1 <= |a_1| <= 2) g_lo(T_R) / (|S^{d-1}| T_R^(d-1)) > 0,
uniformly in |x| <= R and |w| <= R. Measurability of the conditional densities is that of Gaussian kernels composed with
continuous maps; no continuity of phi' is used (only the bounds m <= sigma' <= L). QED

## Theorem 1 (step 1 of target 3)
Under class (A), s > 0 and (S_d), the chain x_{k+1} = Psi_k(x_k) on R^d has a unique invariant probability pi, and for
every p in (0, alpha):
  (i)  E_pi |x|^p < oo;
  (ii) there are C, rho < 1 with sup_{|f| <= 1 + |.|^p} |E_x f(x_n) - pi(f)| <= C (1 + |x|^p) rho^n;
  (iii) pi has a density bounded below by a positive constant on every ball; in particular supp pi = R^d.

Proof. Lemma 2 gives the drift PV <= gamma_p V + K_p. Every sublevel set {V <= R'} is a ball, and by Lemma 3 it carries
a minorization by a multiple of Lebesgue measure on that ball, for every R'. These are Assumptions 1 and 2 of
Hairer-Mattingly, "Yet another look at Harris' ergodic theorem for Markov chains" (Progr. Probab. 63, 2011, 109-117),
whose Theorem 1.2 gives a unique invariant measure and geometric convergence in the V-weighted norm, i.e. (ii); (i)
follows by letting n -> oo in P^n V <= gamma_p^n V + K_p/(1 - gamma_p). The same conclusion is Meyn-Tweedie (2nd ed.)
Theorem 15.0.1 (the ball is small, so petite; the minorizing measure charges the ball, so the chain is strongly
aperiodic). For (iii): pi = pi P >= int_{B_R} pi(dx) P(x, .) >= pi(B_R) eps_R Leb(. cap B_R), and pi(B_R) > 0 for R
large. QED

Citation, read on the page (22 Oct 04:4x) in arXiv:0810.2777v1, p.1-2 (src_hm/HM.pdf, sha256 2ea9915ae59ee286):
Assumption 1 is PV <= gamma V + K with V >= 0, gamma in (0,1); Assumption 2 is inf_(x in C) P(x, .) >= alpha nu(.) for a
probability measure nu and some alpha in (0,1), with C = {V <= R} for some R > 2K/(1 - gamma); Theorem 1.2 gives a unique
invariant measure mu and |P^n phi - mu(phi)| <= C rho^n |phi - mu(phi)| in the norm sup |phi|/(1 + V). Ours: V = 1 + |x|^p,
K = K_p, gamma = gamma_p; {V <= R} is the ball of radius (R - 1)^(1/p), and Lemma 3 on that ball gives Assumption 2 with
nu the normalized Lebesgue measure on the ball and alpha = eps Leb(ball) (shrink eps if needed so alpha < 1). Since
1 + V <= 2V, the bound in their norm gives (ii) as stated. The Meyn-Tweedie reference is an alternative and is not relied on.

## What this feeds
Step 2 (Goldie on |x|) needs E_pi |x|^p < oo for p < alpha: that is (i). Step 3 (c0 > 0) needs unbounded support and a
positive density: that is (iii).

## Numbers (t3_step1_check_run1.txt, 4 million draws each)
(d, b, eta) = (3, 2, 0.9): gamma = -0.044, alpha = 0.358, h < 1 on (0, alpha), E xi^2 = 1.6295 against 1.6300.
(2, 1, 0.8): gamma = -0.065, alpha = 0.400, E xi^2 = 1.9624 against 1.9600.
(5, 4, 1.0): gamma = +0.008, so (S_d) FAILS although eta exceeds the alpha < 2 threshold 2b/(b+d+1) = 0.8; the
alpha < 2 window for (d, b) = (5, 4) ends below eta = 1. Theorem 1 does not apply there, as it should not.

# T228 target 3, step 2: the radial tail t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) -> c0

claude-b1e26540, 22 Oct 2026 04:1x. Status: draft for review. Uses T3_SETUP.md (Lemma R) and T3_STEP1.md (Theorem 1,
Lemma 1). Hypotheses and notation as in T3_STEP1.md: class (A), s > 0, (S_d) gamma = E log xi < 0, alpha the root of
h(alpha) = E xi^alpha = 1.

## The renewal theorem used
Goldie (1991), Theorem 2.3. Read here in the restatement Jelenkovic-Olvera-Cravioto, "Implicit renewal theory and power
tails on trees", arXiv:1006.3295v5, Theorem 3.1, PDF p.5 (src_goldie/JOC_1006.3295.pdf, sha256 abbfbddf3b348a0c), which
with N = 1 and C_1 = C is Goldie's theorem:
  C >= 0, the law of log C on {C > 0} non-arithmetic; 0 < E C^alpha log C < oo; E C^alpha = 1; E C^beta < oo for some
  0 <= beta < alpha; R >= 0 independent of C with E R^beta < oo for every 0 < beta < alpha; and
      int_0^oo | P(R > t) - P(C R > t) | t^(alpha-1) dt < oo.                                           (G)
  Then P(R > t) ~ H t^(-alpha) with 0 <= H < oo,
      H = (E C^alpha log C)^(-1) int_0^oo v^(alpha-1) [P(R > v) - P(C R > v)] dv.
(Goldie's own page was not read: Project Euclid refuses scripted download. The statement above is JOC's, which they give
as a generalization of Goldie's; for N = 1 nothing else is assumed.)

## Theorem 2 (step 2 of target 3)
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1 (T3_STEP1.md), with x ~ pi,
    t^alpha P_pi(|x| > t) -> c0 := E[ |Psi(x)|^alpha - |M x|^alpha ] / (alpha m_alpha),   m_alpha := E xi^alpha log xi,
where Psi = M x + R(x) is one fresh step independent of x, the expectation is absolutely convergent, and 0 <= c0 < oo.

Proof. Take R := |x_0| with x_0 ~ pi and C := |M_0 x_0| / |x_0| (pi has a density, so x_0 != 0 a.s.).

Independence and law of C. M_0 is independent of x_0, and by Lemma R the law of |M_0 u| is that of xi for every unit u. So
given x_0, C has the law of xi whatever x_0 is: C is independent of R and C =_d xi.

Hypotheses on C. xi has a density on (0, oo) (X ~ chi2_b has a density and xi^2 is a smooth function of (X, Y) with
nonvanishing derivative in Y when d >= 2, in X when d = 1, away from a null set), so log xi is non-arithmetic. Every
positive moment of xi is finite (Lemma 1), which gives E C^beta < oo and E C^alpha log+ C < oo. E C^alpha = h(alpha) = 1.
h is log-convex with h(0) = h(alpha) = 1 and is not constant (xi is not a.s. 1), so h is strictly convex on [0, alpha]
and h'(alpha) = m_alpha > 0; it is finite by the moment bounds. So 0 < m_alpha < oo.

Moments of R. E R^beta = E_pi |x|^beta < oo for every beta < alpha: Theorem 1 (i).

Condition (G). By stationarity |Psi(x_0)| =_d |x_0| = R, and C R = |M_0 x_0|. For nonnegative U, V on one space,
    int_0^oo |P(U > t) - P(V > t)| t^(alpha-1) dt <= E int_0^oo |1(U > t) - 1(V > t)| t^(alpha-1) dt
                                                  = E |U^alpha - V^alpha| / alpha.
Take U = |Psi(x_0)|, V = |M_0 x_0|; then |U - V| <= |R(x_0)| <= B with B as in T3_STEP1.md (B depends on the step's data
only, not on x_0, and has all moments).
  alpha <= 1: |U^alpha - V^alpha| <= |U - V|^alpha <= B^alpha, finite in mean.
  alpha > 1: |U^alpha - V^alpha| <= alpha |U - V| max(U, V)^(alpha-1) <= alpha B (V + B)^(alpha-1)
             <= alpha 2^((alpha-2)^+) [ B V^(alpha-1) + B^alpha ].
  Condition on x_0 = x. The pair (M_0, B) is independent of x_0, so by Hoelder with exponents alpha and alpha/(alpha-1),
      E[ B |M_0 x|^(alpha-1) ] <= (E B^alpha)^(1/alpha) (E |M_0 x|^alpha)^((alpha-1)/alpha) = (E B^alpha)^(1/alpha) |x|^(alpha-1),
  using E|M_0 x|^alpha = h(alpha) |x|^alpha = |x|^alpha. Integrating, the bound is (E B^alpha)^(1/alpha) E_pi |x|^(alpha-1),
  finite by Theorem 1 (i) since alpha - 1 < alpha.
So E|U^alpha - V^alpha| < oo and (G) holds.

The theorem gives P_pi(|x| > t) ~ H t^(-alpha). Since E|U^alpha - V^alpha| < oo, Fubini applies to the signed integrand:
int_0^oo v^(alpha-1) [1(U > v) - 1(V > v)] dv = (U^alpha - V^alpha)/alpha pointwise, so
    H = E[ |Psi(x_0)|^alpha - |M_0 x_0|^alpha ] / (alpha m_alpha) = c0.
H >= 0 is part of the theorem's conclusion. QED

Note. What is NOT used: nothing about the direction x/|x|, and no matrix renewal theory (Kesten, Alsmeyer-Mentemeier).
The rotation invariance of the data makes the norm a one-dimensional implicit renewal problem exactly. If c0 > 0 (step 3),
then E_pi |x|^alpha = oo, so the moment range in Theorem 1 (i) is sharp.

## What remains
Step 3: c0 > 0. The theorem gives only c0 >= 0, and c0 = 0 is not excluded by anything above. Plan as in T3_SETUP.md:
a scalar lower chain r_{k+1} = (xi_k r_k - B'_k)^+ with iid pairs (Lemma R), started inside the full support of pi
(Theorem 1 (iii)), and a Cramer-Lundberg lower bound for the tilted walk sum log xi_j; compare ABB Proposition 8.1.

## Citation status
- JOC Theorem 3.1, PDF p.5, read on the page (arXiv v5). Goldie 1991 Thm 2.3 itself: not read (download blocked);
  the claim rests on JOC's statement, which is a stated generalization proved in that paper.
- The comparison inequality for (G) is proved above in one line, so Goldie's Lemma 9.4 is not needed.

name: w688_target1/proofs/T228_A_v1.md
content:
# T228 target 1: scalar asymptotically linear SGD
Version v1: source-checked and submitted for external review; acceptance pending. Author: codex-w688.
Classification: literature-based application, with an explicit stability repair. No claim of a new general renewal theorem or of solving unrestricted neural-network SGD.

## Statement and missing hypothesis
Fix b in {1,2,...}, eta>0, s>0, x* in R. Let sigma(z)=z+phi(z) satisfy class (A) in the dossier. Use independent fresh Gaussian a_i and eps_i at every update and y_i=sigma(a_i x*)+eps_i. In addition require
    lambda(eta,b) = E log|1-(eta/b)Q| < 0,  Q~chi-square_b.                 (S)
Then there is a unique stationary probability pi, the chain is V-geometrically ergodic for some V(x)=1+|x|^p, and
    lim t^alpha pi((t,infinity)) = lim t^alpha pi((-infinity,-t)) = c > 0,
where alpha is the unique positive root
    E|1-(eta/b)Q|^alpha=1.
In particular lim t^alpha pi{|x|>t}=2c>0. For each fixed b there is a nonempty open interval immediately above eta0=2b/(b+2) on which (S) holds and alpha<2.

The dossier omits (S). We prove the intended stable-step statement, not an assertion for every step size. The literal root assertion fails at b=2, eta=100, even for the genuinely nonlinear phi(z)=tanh(z)/2; see the separate witness below.

## 1. Uniform remainder and moments
Put r=sup|phi'|<1, m=1-r>0, L=1+r, H=sup|phi|, and D=sup|z phi'(z)|. For one sample z=ax,
    sigma'(ax)(sigma(ax)-y)a
      = a^2 x + a[z phi'(z)+(1+phi'(z))(phi(z)-y)].
Consequently Psi(x)=Mx+R(x), with M=1-(eta/b)sum a_i^2 and
    |R(x)| <= B0 := (eta/b)sum |a_i|[D+L(H+|y_i|)]                    (1)
for every real x, using the SAME random B0 for all x. Let B=1+B0.
Since |y_i|<=|x*||a_i|+H+|eps_i|, B has moments of every positive order. This argument does not require independence of B and M, nor independence of R(x) and x. The maps are continuous (indeed C^1).

M has a density on (-infinity,1), positive throughout that interval. Therefore P(M=0)=0, both P(M>0) and P(M<0) are positive, and log|M| has an absolutely continuous law. Near zero the density of M is bounded, so E|log|M||<infinity. All positive moments of |M| and E[|M|^q |log|M||] for q>0 are finite.

## 2. Root, drift, irreducibility, and geometric ergodicity
Write h(q)=E|M|^q. Its right derivative at zero is lambda<0. The function log h is strictly convex because log|M| is nonconstant; h(0)=1 and h(q) tends to infinity (P(|M|>2)>0). Thus there is exactly one alpha>0 with h(alpha)=1, and h(p)<1 for every 0<p<alpha.

Choose 0<p<min(alpha,1). Subadditivity and (1) give
    P V(x) <= 1+h(p)|x|^p+E B0^p = h(p)V(x)+C.
Choose gamma in (h(p),1). For a sufficiently large compact C0=[-K,K] this implies
    P V <= gamma V + d 1_C0.                                      (2)

Here is a direct compact minorization, rather than an inference from nonzero variance alone. Conditional on the a_i, Psi(x) is normal, with mean
    mu(x,a)=x-(eta/b)sum a_i sigma'(a_i x)
                                  [sigma(a_i x)-sigma(a_i x*)]
and variance
    v(x,a)=(eta s/b)^2 sum a_i^2 sigma'(a_i x)^2.                   (3)
Restrict to E={1<=a_i<=2 for all i}, an event with positive probability. On x in C0 and a in [1,2]^b, the mean is uniformly bounded by continuity, while
    eta^2 s^2 m^2/b <= v(x,a) <= 4 eta^2 s^2 L^2/b.
For z in C0 these mean and variance bounds give a strictly positive uniform lower bound on the conditional normal density. Integrating over E gives
    P(x,A)>=delta Leb(A intersect C0), x in C0.
Enlarge K if necessary so C0 has nonzero length. Thus C0 is a one-step small set whose minorizing measure charges C0; this gives aperiodicity. For each x and almost every a, (3) is positive, so P(x,A)>0 for every Borel A of positive Lebesgue measure. The chain is Lebesgue-irreducible.

The standard irreducible, aperiodic Foster-Lyapunov theorem applied to (2) yields positive Harris recurrence, a unique invariant probability pi, pi(V)<infinity, and constants C<infinity, rho<1 such that
    ||P^n(x,.)-pi||_V <= C V(x) rho^n.
One may use Meyn-Tweedie's geometric-drift theorem (Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability, Theorem 15.0.1 and its V-uniform formulation). In particular this establishes the requested geometric ergodicity without assuming E log Lip(Psi)<0.

For every nonempty open interval I, P(x,I)>0 for all x, hence
    pi(I)=integral P(x,I) pi(dx)>0.                               (4)
The support of pi is all of R, in particular unbounded in BOTH directions.

## 3. Exact literature theorem and all its inputs
Use Alsmeyer-Brofferio-Buraczewski (ABB), arXiv:2102.02299, Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 8.1; published in Annals of Applied Probability 33 (2023), 161-199, doi:10.1214/22-AAP1812. The arXiv locators are Theorem 2.1, equations (12)-(16), PDF pages 6-7; Proposition 8.1, PDF page 36. The theorem treats continuous random maps satisfying the two uniform asymptotic-linear bounds (3), with slopes A^- and A^+, a two-state irreducible sign chain, the positive spectral-root condition (12), moments (13), and Markov nonarithmetic condition (14). Proposition 8.1 supplies strict positivity for unbounded stationary support.

Here set A^-=A^+=M, with B from (1). This is a direct ALIFS, even though R depends on x. With signs ordered (-,+), define
    d(q)=E[|M|^q 1_{M>0}], o(q)=E[|M|^q 1_{M<0}].
ABB's matrix is
    P(q) = [[d(q),o(q)],[o(q),d(q)]].
Both entries are positive. Its Perron eigenvalue is h(q)=d(q)+o(q); left Perron eigenvector normalized to sum one is u=(1/2,1/2), with right eigenvector (1,1). In particular it is the irreducible case, and (12) is precisely h(alpha)=1, already proved. Both required slope log moments and E B^alpha are finite by section 1.

Verify the stronger MARKOV nonarithmetic condition (14), not only scalar nonarithmetic. Under the alpha-tilted stationary sign law, the conditional increment log|M| along either self transition is absolutely continuous on (-infinity,0), since 0<M<1 there. These transitions have positive tilted probability. For any lattice d Z and any sign offsets a_-,a_+, a self transition cancels the offsets; an absolutely continuous increment belongs to that lattice with probability zero. Thus the lattice event in (14) cannot have probability one. No independence of signs and magnitudes is asserted or needed.

Theorem 2.1 therefore gives finite nonnegative tail constants. Proposition 8.1 applies because of (4), and makes both constants strictly positive. Finally equation (16), together with u_- = u_+ =1/2, gives C_-=C_+=c. This proves the exact exponent AND the positivity step that GSZ's short restatement does not justify.

## 4. A nonempty alpha<2 regime without numerical quadrature
Chi-square moments give E Q=b and E Q^2=b(b+2), so
    h(2)=1-2 eta+eta^2(1+2/b).
At eta0=2b/(b+2), h(2)=1. Strict Jensen, applied to the nonconstant random variable M^2, gives
    lambda(eta0,b)=(1/2)E log M^2 < (1/2)log E M^2 =0.             (5)
All quantities are finite.

For completeness lambda is continuous in eta near eta0. Away from the moving zero Q=b/eta, dominated convergence uses Gaussian/exponential tail decay and log(1+C Q). The zero stays in a compact subinterval of (0,infinity), where the chi-square density is bounded uniformly. On a small interval around this zero, a change of variable u=1-eta Q/b bounds the absolute log contribution uniformly by a constant times integral_{|u|<epsilon}|log|u||du, which tends to zero. This gives the necessary uniform integrability and continuity.

By (5), (S) persists on (eta0,eta0+delta) for some delta>0. On this interval h(2)>1. Since h(q)<1 below its unique positive root and h(q)>1 above it, alpha<2 there. This proves a whole nonlinear class on a nonempty parameter interval for EVERY b.

## 5. Literal statement failure if stability is not added
Take b=2, eta=100, phi(z)=tanh(z)/2, x*=0, s=1. This phi satisfies all class-(A) requirements, including bounded z phi''(z). Now U=Q/2 has Exp(1) law and M=1-100U.

For |M|<1, its density is <=1/100. Hence the entire negative log contribution is at least
    -(1/100) integral_{-1}^1 |log|m|| dm = -2/100.
On U>=1, |M|>=99 and P(U>=1)=exp(-1). All other log contributions outside |M|<1 are nonnegative. Thus
    E log|M| >= exp(-1) log(99)-0.02 >0.
Jensen gives h(q)>=exp(q E log|M|)>1 for every q>0. There is no positive root, contrary to unrestricted part (3). This is a counterexample to the literal unqualified target, not a new linear-tail result. It does not by itself assert absence of every possible stationary distribution. The stable-step theorem above addresses the intended model instead of ending with this missing-hypothesis objection.

## 6. Scope, source audit, and review
No global Lipschitz contraction is used or claimed. No simulations are used as proof. s>0 is essential to the full-support/minorization argument; without it a common fixed point can invalidate positivity. The case phi=0 is included but is already settled, and no novelty credit is sought for it. An example with genuine nonlinearity is phi(z)=tanh(z)/2.

GSZ Theorem 1 omits a positivity assumption present in Mirek's Theorem 1.8. Mirek also has extra hypotheses; its Theorem 1.15 concerns stable limits of sums, not the stationary-tail positivity assertion needed here. We do not certify Mirek's hypotheses for this SGD map or use GSZ's restatement. ABB is the source that closes this target's stated obstruction. This is a literature-based application; a claim of being the first nonlinear SGD example requires a separate literature novelty search and is not made here.

Review request: independently check the conditional-normal minorization; applicability of ABB Proposition 8.1 without hidden global contraction; the sign-matrix nonarithmetic condition and equality of constants; and whether the lead accepts adding (S) to the dossier. No external review has yet accepted this version.

# Author self-audit v1

This is not independent external review. Source snapshots and hashes verified for all five references. ABB Theorem 2.1 equations (12)-(16), Proposition 8.1 and standing continuity/bounded-remainder assumptions read in full. The theorem needs no mean global Lipschitz contraction. M is nonzero almost surely, both sign transitions occur, all slope and remainder moments exist, and the self-transition continuous log law verifies the full Markov lattice condition. The invariant law has full support by conditional Gaussian transitions. Tail constants are equal by the symmetric Perron vector, without assuming the finite-body stationary law is symmetric.

The Foster drift is for a fractional exponent below both alpha and one. Compact minorization explicitly restricts all inputs to [1,2]; a mere positive-variance assertion is not used as a minorization proof. s>0 and sup|phi prime|<1 are indispensable to this check.

The b=2, eta=100 witness disproves only the unqualified root assertion. The stable theorem states its mean-log restriction openly. A nonempty alpha<2 interval is proved by strict Jensen and continuity; quadrature is only a check. Numerical checks also compare the exact second moment with a separate integral and check the nonlinear update algebra and uniform bound at 1600 input states. No sampled tail plot is treated as proof.
